name: Hasura DDN
license: Proprietary service; the v3 engine and connectors are Apache 2.0
summary: Hasura Data Delivery Network: you describe models, commands, relationships and permissions as metadata, and a Rust engine serves them as one GraphQL (or JSON:API) API over databases and code reached through data connectors.
intro: A data connector introspects a source, such as PostgreSQL, ClickHouse, DuckDB or your own TypeScript functions, and the `ddn` CLI turns that into metadata objects in your repo: models that read data, commands that modify it, relationships that join it (even across sources) and permissions that protect it. The CLI builds the metadata into an immutable build, and the v3 engine serves it as a GraphQL API with filtering, sorting, pagination, aggregations and subscriptions, plus a JSON:API interface that uses the same permissions. The engine never runs SQL itself: it plans each query and sends an intermediate representation to the connectors, which speak the open NDC specification. Authentication stays outside: a JWT or a webhook supplies session variables, and the engine checks them against your permissions.

You can run it three ways. Hosted Hasura DDN deploys the API on Hasura’s global infrastructure with autoscaling and its control plane (build versions, schema registry, breaking-change detection, traces). Private DDN puts the data plane in your own VPC or on dedicated infrastructure under an enterprise contract. Or you self-host the open-source v3 engine and connectors with Docker, without the control plane. Pricing is per active model, meaning any model or command called more than 1,000 times a month: Free costs $0 with unlimited models and one developer, Base starts at $5 and Advanced at $30 per active model per month, and hosting third-party or code connectors costs $0.075 per vCPU-hour. In June 2025 Hasura made PromptQL, an AI data-access product, its focus and said DDN and the v2 GraphQL Engine would continue to be hosted and maintained.
strengths: No resolvers to write: introspection generates models and commands, and the engine adds filtering, sorting, pagination and aggregations, nested across relationships
Joins across sources: a relationship can link a PostgreSQL table to a ClickHouse table, and one query follows it
Permissions and the schema are versioned metadata, so each build is immutable and can be diffed for breaking changes before release
The engine (Rust), the NDC spec and the connectors are open source under Apache 2.0, and you can write your own connector with SDKs in Rust, TypeScript, Python or Go
limits: A new engine and metadata format: v2 projects need a migration, and v3 was in alpha until 2024 and generally available only from August 2024
Self-hosting the engine leaves out the control plane: no built-in CI/CD or build versioning, schema registry or API analytics
Per-model pricing can grow quickly with many busy models, and Private DDN needs an enterprise contract
Hasura made PromptQL its focus in June 2025; it says DDN will continue to be hosted and maintained, but it is no longer the headline product

snippet.title: From a Postgres database to a GraphQL API with the DDN CLI
source: ddn supergraph init my-project && cd my-project
ddn connector init my_pg -i          # interactive: choose the PostgreSQL connector
ddn connector introspect my_pg       # read tables, views and functions
ddn model add my_pg '*'              # models that read data
ddn command add my_pg '*'            # commands that modify data
ddn supergraph build local && ddn run docker-start
ddn console --local                  # GraphiQL and the metadata explorer
ddn project init                     # then deploy to hosted DDN

story: Hasura launched its GraphQL Engine in July 2018 as an open-source product that gave any Postgres database instant realtime GraphQL APIs, with a console for creating tables and running queries. Versions 1 and 2 were written in Haskell, and v2 added data connectors so that query generation for more databases could live outside the engine.

At HasuraCon in June 2023 co-founder and CEO Tanmai Gopal announced the Data Delivery Network: a re-architected engine with zero cold start that could run on an edge network, metadata based on a new Open Data Domain Specification, and a Native Data Connector specification for any source. In December 2023 Hasura open-sourced the v3 engine, now written in Rust, together with the NDC spec and its first connectors. DDN entered beta on 4 April 2024 and became generally available on 20 August 2024, pitched as a metadata-driven data access layer.

On 2 June 2025 Gopal announced PromptQL, an AI platform that writes data-access programs from natural language, as the company’s new focus and the “spiritual successor to GraphQL”. Hasura said the GraphQL Engine and DDN would continue to be hosted and maintained; the v3 engine in the `graphql-engine` repository was still receiving commits in August 2026.

choices.why: Hasura said the rewrite was about performance, scalability and reliability for cloud-native APIs, and about tapping the wider Rust community.
In v2 the SQL generation for PostgreSQL, SQL Server and BigQuery was tied to the core engine; with NDC every source is a separate, forkable connector, and the engine only sends it a query plan.

choices.choice: Metadata as the API’s source code
choices.why: The launch post argued that if Hasura is given resources, methods, relationships and authorization policies as metadata, it can provision the API itself, so governance comes from the same files that define the API.

choices.choice: Price per active model, not per request
choices.why: The beta post set the goal that APIs should not get more expensive as usage grows, so DDN bills for models that are used, with unlimited requests.
